question.text: Refinancing a loan is advantageous when:

answer.text: A lower cost loan is available to repay the existing costlier loan
The borrower wants to increase the loan amount
The borrower has missed several EMI payments

explanation.text: The Logic: Refinancing makes sense when a lower-cost loan is available to repay an existing costlier loan. The benefit should be evaluated using the lower interest rate, the tenure remaining, and any processing or other charges so that the net saving is positive. The Trap: Refinancing when rates have increased would actually raise the cost. It is beneficial only when cheaper alternatives are available. Note: Borrowers should compute the breakeven period over which the interest savings recover the switch-related charges before deciding to refinance.
